title: अध्याय १०२

items.text:
अथ द्व्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः
मार्तण्डोत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
items.tr:
atha dvyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ
mārtaṇḍotpattivarṇanam

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ततः स्वतेजसस्तस्मादाविर्भूतो विभावसुः ।
अदृश्यत तदादित्यस्तप्तताम्रोपमप्रभः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ svatejasastasmādāvirbhūto vibhāvasuḥ |
adṛśyata tadādityastaptatāmropamaprabhaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
अथ तां प्रणतां देवीं तस्य संदर्शनान्मुने ।
प्राह भास्वन्वृणुष्वेष्टवरं मत्तो यमिच्छसि ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
atha tāṃ praṇatāṃ devīṃ tasya saṃdarśanānmune |
prāha bhāsvanvṛṇuṣveṣṭavaraṃ matto yamicchasi || 2 ||

items.text:
प्रणता शिरसा सा च जानुपीडितमेदिनी ।
प्रत्युवाच विवस्वन्तं वरदं समुपस्थितम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
praṇatā śirasā sā ca jānupīḍitamedinī |
pratyuvāca vivasvantaṃ varadaṃ samupasthitam || 3 ||

items.text:
देव प्रसीद पुत्राणां हृतं त्रिभुवनं मम ।
यज्ञभागाश्च दैत्यैश्च दानवैश्च बलाधिकैः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
deva prasīda putrāṇāṃ hṛtaṃ tribhuvanaṃ mama |
yajñabhāgāśca daityaiśca dānavaiśca balādhikaiḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
तन्निमित्तं प्रसादं त्वं कुरुष्व मम गोपते ।
अंशेन तेषां भ्रातृत्वं गत्वा नाशय तद्रिपून् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tannimittaṃ prasādaṃ tvaṃ kuruṣva mama gopate |
aṃśena teṣāṃ bhrātṛtvaṃ gatvā nāśaya tadripūn || 5 ||

items.text:
यथा मे तनया भूयो यज्ञभागभुजः प्रभो ।
भवेयुरधिपाश्चैव त्रैलोक्यस्य दिवाकर ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
yathā me tanayā bhūyo yajñabhāgabhujaḥ prabho |
bhaveyuradhipāścaiva trailokyasya divākara || 6 ||

items.text:
तथानुकम्पां पुत्राणां सुप्रसन्नो रवे मम ।
कुरु प्रपन्नार्तिहर स्थितिकर्त्ता त्वमुच्यसे ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tathānukampāṃ putrāṇāṃ suprasanno rave mama |
kuru prapannārtihara sthitikarttā tvamucyase || 7 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ततस्तामाह भगवान्भास्करो वारितस्करः ।
प्रणतामदितिं विप्र प्रसादसुमुखो विभुः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tatastāmāha bhagavānbhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ |
praṇatāmaditiṃ vipra prasādasumukho vibhuḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
सहस्रांशेन ते गर्भे सम्भूयाहमशेषतः ।
त्वत्पुत्रशत्रूनदिते नाशयाम्याशु निर्वृतः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
sahasrāṃśena te garbhe sambhūyāhamaśeṣataḥ |
tvatputraśatrūnadite nāśayāmyāśu nirvṛtaḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्भास्वानन्तर्द्धानमुपागमत् ।
निवृत्ता सापि तपसः संतृप्ताखिलवाञ्छिता ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
ityuktvā bhagavānbhāsvānantarddhānamupāgamat |
nivṛttā sāpi tapasaḥ saṃtṛptākhilavāñchitā || 10 ||

items.text:
ततो रश्मिसहस्रात्तु सौषुम्नाख्यो रवेः करः ।
विप्रावतारं संचक्रे देवमातुरथोदरे ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
tato raśmisahasrāttu sauṣumnākhyo raveḥ karaḥ |
viprāvatāraṃ saṃcakre devamāturathodare || 11 ||

items.text:
कृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणादीनि सा च चक्रे समाहिता ।
शुचिः संधारयामास दिव्यं गर्भमिति द्विज ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīni sā ca cakre samāhitā |
śuciḥ saṃdhārayāmāsa divyaṃ garbhamiti dvija || 12 ||

items.text:
ततस्तां कश्यपः प्राह किञ्चित्कोपप्लुताक्षरम् ।
किं मारयसि गर्भाण्डमिति नित्योपवासिनी ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
tatastāṃ kaśyapaḥ prāha kiñcitkopaplutākṣaram |
kiṃ mārayasi garbhāṇḍamiti nityopavāsinī || 13 ||

items.text:
सा च तं प्राह गर्भाण्डमेतत्पश्येति कोपना ।
न मारितं विपक्षाणां मृत्यवे तद्भविष्यति ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
sā ca taṃ prāha garbhāṇḍametatpaśyeti kopanā |
na māritaṃ vipakṣāṇāṃ mṛtyave tadbhaviṣyati || 14 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा तं तदा गर्भमुत्ससर्ज्ज सुरारणिः ।
जाज्वल्यमानं तेजोभिः पत्युर्वचनकोपिता ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktvā taṃ tadā garbhamutsasarjja surāraṇiḥ |
jājvalyamānaṃ tejobhiḥ patyurvacanakopitā || 15 ||

items.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा कश्यपो गर्भमुद्यद्भास्करवर्च्चसम् ।
तुष्टाव प्रणतो भूत्वा ऋग्भिराद्याभिरादरात् ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaśyapo garbhamudyadbhāskaravarccasam |
tuṣṭāva praṇato bhūtvā ṛgbhirādyābhirādarāt || 16 ||

items.text:
संस्तूयमानः स तदा गर्भाण्डात्प्रकटोऽभवत् ।
पद्मपत्रसवर्णाभस्तेजसा व्याप्तदिङ्मुखः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
saṃstūyamānaḥ sa tadā garbhāṇḍātprakaṭo'bhavat |
padmapatrasavarṇābhastejasā vyāptadiṅmukhaḥ || 17 ||

items.text:
अथान्तरिक्षादाभाष्य कश्यपं मुनिसत्तमम् ।
सतोयमेघगम्भीरवागुवाचाशरीरिणी ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
athāntarikṣādābhāṣya kaśyapaṃ munisattamam |
satoyameghagambhīravāguvācāśarīriṇī || 18 ||

items.text:
मारितं ते यतः प्रोक्तमेतदण्डं त्वया मुने ।
तस्मान्मुने सुतस्तेऽयं मार्त्तण्डाख्यो भविष्यति ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
māritaṃ te yataḥ proktametadaṇḍaṃ tvayā mune |
tasmānmune sutaste'yaṃ mārttaṇḍākhyo bhaviṣyati || 19 ||

items.text:
सूर्याधिकारं च विभुर्जगत्येष करिष्यति ।
हनिष्यत्यसुरांश्चायं यज्ञभागहरानरीन् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
sūryādhikāraṃ ca vibhurjagatyeṣa kariṣyati |
haniṣyatyasurāṃścāyaṃ yajñabhāgaharānarīn || 20 ||

items.text:
देवा निशम्येति वचो गगनात्समुपागमन् ।
प्रहर्षमतुलं याता दानवाश्च हतौजसः ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
devā niśamyeti vaco gaganātsamupāgaman |
praharṣamatulaṃ yātā dānavāśca hataujasaḥ || 21 ||

items.text:
ततो युद्धाय दैतेयानाजुहाव शतक्रतुः ।
सह देवैर्मुदा युक्तो दानवाश्च समभ्ययुः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
tato yuddhāya daiteyānājuhāva śatakratuḥ |
saha devairmudā yukto dānavāśca samabhyayuḥ || 22 ||

items.text:
तेषां युद्धमभूद्घोरं देवानामसुरैः सह ।
शस्त्रास्त्रदीप्तिसंदीप्तं समस्तभुवनान्तरम् ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
teṣāṃ yuddhamabhūdghoraṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha |
śastrāstradīptisaṃdīptaṃ samastabhuvanāntaram || 23 ||

items.text:
तस्मिन्युद्धे भगवता मार्त्तण्डेन निरीक्षिताः ।
तेजसा दह्यमानास्ते भस्मीभूता महासुराः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
tasminyuddhe bhagavatā mārttaṇḍena nirīkṣitāḥ |
tejasā dahyamānāste bhasmībhūtā mahāsurāḥ || 24 ||

items.text:
ततः प्रहर्षमतुलं प्राप्ताः सर्वे दिवौकसः ।
तुष्टुवुस्तेजसा योनिं मार्त्तण्डमदितिं तथा ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ praharṣamatulaṃ prāptāḥ sarve divaukasaḥ |
tuṣṭuvustejasā yoniṃ mārttaṇḍamaditiṃ tathā || 25 ||

items.text:
स्वाधिकारांस्तथा प्राप्ता यज्ञभागांश्च पूर्ववत् ।
भगवानपि मार्तण्डः स्वाधिकारमथाकरोत् ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
svādhikārāṃstathā prāptā yajñabhāgāṃśca pūrvavat |
bhagavānapi mārtaṇḍaḥ svādhikāramathākarot || 26 ||

items.text:
कदम्बपुष्पवद्भास्वानधश्चोर्ध्वं च रश्मिभिः ।
वृत्ताग्निपिण्डसदृशो दध्रे नातिस्फुरद्वपुः ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
kadambapuṣpavadbhāsvānadhaścordhvaṃ ca raśmibhiḥ |
vṛttāgnipiṇḍasadṛśo dadhre nātisphuradvapuḥ || 27 ||

en_summary: Markandeya continues. Then from that light the Sun appeared, glowing like heated copper. As Aditi bowed at the sight of him, he told her to choose whatever boon she wished from him. Bowing her head, with her knees pressed to the ground, she said: the strong daityas and danavas have taken the three worlds and the shares of the sacrifice from her sons; for their sake let him be gracious, take birth with part of himself as their brother and destroy their enemies, so that her sons may again share the sacrifice and rule the three worlds; he is called the remover of the pain of those who take refuge and the one who keeps the world in order. The Sun, gracious, told her he would be born from her womb with a thousandth part of himself and quickly destroy her sons' enemies, and then vanished. Aditi, all her wishes fulfilled, ended her penance. Then, from his thousand rays, the ray of the Sun called Sushumna took birth in the womb of the mother of the gods. With a focused mind she kept hard vows such as krichchhra and chandrayana and carried the divine embryo in purity. Kashyapa, somewhat angry, said to her: why do you kill the embryo (garbhanda) by fasting all the time? She angrily replied: look at this embryo; it is not killed (marita); it will be the death of the enemies. Saying this, the mother of the gods, stung by her husband's words, brought out the embryo, blazing with light. Seeing it shine like the rising sun, Kashyapa bowed and praised it with the first Rig verses. As he praised, the child came out of the egg, coloured like a lotus leaf, his light filling all directions. Then a voice from the sky, deep as a rain cloud, said to Kashyapa: since you called this egg 'killed' (marita), your son will be named Martanda; he will perform the office of the Sun in the world and will kill the asuras, the enemies who took the shares of the sacrifice. Hearing this voice, the gods rejoiced greatly, and the danavas lost their strength. Indra (Shatakratu) joyfully called the daityas to battle with the gods, and the danavas came. There was a terrible war between the gods and the asuras, with weapons and missiles lighting up all the worlds. In that battle the great asuras, looked at by the lord Martanda, were burned by his light and turned to ashes. All the gods, overjoyed, praised Martanda and Aditi; they regained their offices and their shares of the sacrifice as before, and Martanda took up his own office. Like a kadamba flower, with rays going up and down, the Sun took a body like a round ball of fire, not too brilliant.
